R101.note: Reordering the spread so _id and ownerId are assigned last makes the trusted scalar values always win, closing the operator-override on the ownership predicate; extraCriteria can still narrow by other fields as the route intends and nothing else changes.

R102.note: Path containment plus the regex closes traversal, but the ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ allowlist is a new restriction the contract (plugins under ./plugins/*.js) does not call for and rejects names containing a dot or subdirectory that the original resolved.

R103.note: POST plus [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] closes CSRF, but the existing confirmation page's GET link stops working until the view is rewritten as a token-bearing form; the write-up states this openly as a required follow-up outside the change set.

R104.note: Moving uid into the {1} filterArgs placeholder lets JNDI escape it per RFC 4515 with the same search overload and error handling; only the not-found diagnostic now echoes the template ({1}) instead of the raw value, which is inherent to parameterizing and not a functional change.

R105.note: snprintf into message with the >= sizeof truncation check returns -1 on oversized input and produces the identical AUDIT username:action output for inputs that fit, matching the stated contract.

R106.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param('s')/get_result binds the username out-of-band and preserves the same ?array return and null-on-failure paths.

R107.note: Mapping the caller's sort key to fixed code-defined fragments in the service means only literal strings reach ${sort}; tenantId stays bound, created_at default preserved, and the silent fallback for unknown keys is stated and consistent with the contract's allowlist requirement.

R108.note: Using detected.ext from the same magic-number sniff that gated acceptance ties the on-disk extension to the verified type; the only other change (stored id extension now derived from content, e.g. .jpeg becomes .jpg) is stated and blocks no legitimate upload.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES/UTF-8 at the render point encodes both fields correctly for element content; the explanation's claim that pre-8.1 PHP defaults to ISO-8859-1 is wrong (UTF-8 default since 5.4) but the code is correct.

R110.note: Explicit channelIndex >= size() check before operator[] drops out-of-range updates without changing behaviour for valid channels 0-7; the reasoning for rejecting .at() is sound for a void control-loop function.

R111.note: fullmatch on a strict dot-atom pattern excludes <, >, space, CR and LF so no same-line parameter injection reaches docmd, but the regex is a new restriction that rejects valid RFC 5321 addresses the original forwarded (single-label domains like user@localhost, quoted local parts, address literals) and turns them into an uncaught ValueError.

R112.note: One $n placeholder per element with ids passed as the pg parameter array binds every value out-of-band; the query shape, empty-array behaviour (IN () still errors as before) and return value are unchanged.

R113.note: pathinfo final-extension check with strict in_array closes the double-extension bypass, getimagesize confirms image content, and the random server-side filename removes the client name from the path; the loss of the original recognizable filename and the changed returned path are stated plainly and do not stop a legitimate image upload.

R114.note: push_back into the reserved vector closes the out-of-bounds write, but clamping to std::min(count, fields.size()) silently truncates when count exceeds the source, which the stated contract explicitly says must be rejected or reported rather than silently truncated.
